title: Mould in a Berlin Flat - Quick Summary
items: **Relative humidity is the number that misleads you.** What decides whether a window dries the room is grams of water per cubic metre. A living room at **20 °C and 60 percent** holds **10.4 g/m³**, and outdoor air only helps if it carries less.

**In January airing removes 5.5 g per cubic metre. In August it adds 0.7.** Ten years of Deutscher Wetterdienst hourly data for Berlin-Tempelhof show outdoor air averaging **4.9 g/m³ in January**, **8.3 in October**, **9.6 in September** and **11.1 in August**. Across the full month-by-hour grid, **49 of 288 hours put water into that room** and another 68 shift less than half a gram.

**In summer the afternoon is drier than dawn.** Berlin air at 06:00 in July carries **11.3 g/m³**, at 16:00 only **10.2**. In August the gap is 11.6 against 10.4. Airing early because it feels fresh is the wrong move from June to August. In winter the hour barely matters at all.

**Mould starts about 3.4 °C before you see water.** The Umweltbundesamt puts the growth threshold at **70 to 80 percent humidity at the material surface**, and materials need not look wet. In a 20 °C, 60 percent room, any surface below **15.4 °C** is at that line, while visible condensation waits until **12.0 °C**.

**Berlin's retrofit moved the job onto the tenant.** About **a quarter of Berlin flats predate 1918**. An untouched old flat leaks roughly **0.5 air changes per hour**, twelve free changes a day, and the Umweltbundesamt's model bedroom then needs only one morning airing. Fit tight windows without touching the walls and infiltration drops to about **0.1 per hour**, where the guide says the required frequency **is barely achieved in practice**.

**A cold outer wall is usually not a legal defect.** The Bundesgerichtshof ruled on **5 December 2018** that thermal bridges are no defect when the building matches the standards in force when it was built, and overturned a 20 percent rent reduction. The lower court had held **twice daily for up to ten minutes** to be the fair limit of what a tenant can be asked to do.

**My move: work the calendar, not the lease.** Until mid October cut the sources, because the window is doing under a gram. From mid October to March, wide open windows on opposite sides for five minutes, twice a day. Tilting the window instead chills the reveal, which is exactly where Berlin mould begins.
